sources.title: Merriam-Webster: retain (general, medical and legal sections)

facts.statement: Continued possession/use, including deposits, customs and rights.
facts.source_detail: General 1a and dictionary examples; synonym discussion adds resistance to loss.

facts.statement: Keeping employees; engaging paid professional services.
facts.source_detail: General 1b; examples include attorney and firm + purpose infinitive.

facts.statement: Keeping facts in memory.
facts.source_detail: General 1c.

facts.statement: Secure/intact holding, illustrated by moisture and heat.
facts.source_detail: General 2; Kids Definition 2.

facts.statement: Medical retain includes holding fluids inside.
facts.source_detail: Medical Definition 1; does not by itself specify a disease or mechanism.

facts.statement: Keep concerns possession/control; withhold concerns refusal/restraint in giving.
facts.source_detail: Choose the Right Synonym, not a claim about every context.

facts.statement: Middle English through Anglo-French; Latin retinēre, re- plus tenēre.
facts.source_detail: Word History; MW first-known-use dating is 15th century, not a consensus exact date.

facts.statement: British and American /rɪˈteɪn/; retains /rɪˈteɪnz/, retained /rɪˈteɪnd/, retaining /rɪˈteɪnɪŋ/.
facts.source_detail: Pronunciation and expanded Verb Forms.

facts.statement: Retain is labelled rather formal.
facts.source_detail: Headword register label; no numeric or genre-frequency claim.

facts.statement: Examples include control, original character, titles, political seats and talent.
facts.source_detail: Sense 1 and Extra Examples; parliamentary seat is explicit.

facts.statement: Holding/containing includes soil moisture and stored computer information.
facts.source_detail: Sense 2; computer-memory example is passive.

facts.statement: Human memory/facts is included.
facts.source_detail: Sense 2 figurative example.

facts.statement: Professional payment may be regular or advance; services-of and person-as-role are attested.
facts.source_detail: Sense 3 and sense 1 Extra Examples respectively.

facts.statement: Late Middle English via Anglo-Norman/Old French; Latin re- back plus tenere hold.
facts.source_detail: Word Origin; no claim that all modern senses historically arose in article order.

sources.title: Collins: retain (COBUILD, Collins English Dictionary, Webster’s New World)

facts.statement: Holding contents, keeping a fixed condition, and fixing position.
facts.source_detail: British senses 2/4; Webster’s New World American 2/3.

facts.statement: Keeping rooms available for future use is recorded.
facts.source_detail: British sense 5; does not establish a blanket region label or high frequency.

facts.statement: Engagement can be for a specified trial.
facts.source_detail: COBUILD law sense 2, purpose-for example; not limited to pre-existing employment.

facts.statement: Requiring a student to repeat a school grade is marked US education.
facts.source_detail: Webster’s New World American sense 7; not a generic enrollment meaning.

facts.statement: Retain a customer appears as a collocation heading.
facts.source_detail: COBUILD Collocations; no numerical collocation frequency inferred.

facts.statement: The entry also records selling-race buyback and jockey service reservation; retainable and retainment appear.
facts.source_detail: British senses 7/8 and Derived forms; recorded for coverage accounting, not silently added to the candidate.

sources.title: Random House retain, American section hosted by Collins

facts.statement: A cloth keeping its color illustrates retain.
facts.source_detail: American segment credited to Penguin Random House, sense 3; separate from Webster’s New World.

facts.statement: Retention covers continued keeping, liquid/heat containment and memory; staff and fluid are exemplified.
facts.source_detail: Senses 1–3; origin is French/Latin retentio from retinere, not simply an English suffix invented here.

facts.statement: Retentive describes holding capacity, including moisture and memory; retentively and retentiveness are listed.
facts.source_detail: Headword, run-ons and etymology from Latin retinēre family; Japanese glosses are editorial.

facts.statement: Retainer includes servant/employee, holding device, orthodontic appliance, professional engagement and fee.
facts.source_detail: Noun (1) senses 1/3; noun (2) senses 1/2. Does not identify any hired lawyer as the usual referent of the noun.

facts.statement: Retainer includes availability payment, post-orthodontic appliance and an old-fashioned long-serving household servant.
facts.source_detail: Senses 1/3/4; monthly payment example. Dental sense is marked North American in this dictionary.

facts.statement: Retainer can designate a lawyer compensation agreement reserving availability or future services.
facts.source_detail: Opening and discussion of agreement varieties; used only for the lexical agreement sense, not legal advice.

facts.statement: Retaining is a specialist attributive adjective for keeping something positioned; retaining wall is exemplified.
facts.source_detail: Only-before-noun label and sense 1.

sources.title: Cambridge Business English Dictionary: retained earnings

facts.statement: Retained earnings are company profits kept rather than distributed as dividends.
facts.source_detail: Accounting/finance definition; accessed through original-publisher search result after direct fetch failed. Reinvestment is illustrated; no financial advice or actual company claim.

facts.statement: Tenure includes a period/right of holding property or office and traces to Latin tenēre.
facts.source_detail: General sense 1 and Word History.

facts.statement: Detain can hold back or confine; its etymology includes Latin de- plus tenēre.
facts.source_detail: General senses and Word History.

facts.statement: Contain can have something within; Latin continēre contains con- plus tenēre.
facts.source_detail: General 1 and Word History.

sources.title: NIDDK: Definition & Facts of Urinary Retention

facts.statement: Urinary retention includes inability to empty the bladder completely, whether acute or chronic.
facts.source_detail: What is urinary retention? Does not entail total inability to pass any urine in every case.

sources.title: NIDDK: Symptoms & Causes of Urinary Retention

facts.statement: Temporary urinary retention can occur after surgery.
facts.source_detail: Surgery paragraph; supports scenario plausibility, not the invented patient or every cause.

sources.title: NIDDK: Your Kidneys & How They Work

facts.statement: Kidneys remove wastes and excess water to produce urine.
facts.source_detail: Opening explanation and urinary-system description; urine is the carrier/output, not identical to every waste product.

sources.title: MSD Manual: Overview of Sodium’s Role in the Body

facts.statement: Normal volume regulation can increase renal sodium retention and conserve water; sodium exits in urine and sweat.
facts.source_detail: Controlling blood volume and opening physiology paragraphs; supports non-pathological regulation, not a diagnosis.

facts.statement: Low renal blood flow is associated with increased renin; the described hormonal system makes kidneys retain salt and water.
facts.source_detail: What does renin do? and common conditions; the candidate example condenses this mechanism and uses may.

facts.statement: Some medications can cause fluid retention; disease contexts can also involve fluid accumulation.
facts.source_detail: Causes paragraph explicitly mentions NSAIDs; used for possibility, not a universal medication claim or the candidate’s unnamed condition.

sources.title: MSD Manual Professional: Overview of Pharmacokinetics

facts.statement: Pharmacokinetic elimination comprises metabolism and excretion.
facts.source_detail: Formulas Defining Basic Pharmacokinetic Parameters table: Elimination category. This is drug disappearance, not necessarily physical removal of unchanged drug.

facts.statement: Grade retention is remaining in the same grade across school years; academic readiness or behavior can be involved.
facts.source_detail: Indicator 15 introductory text and endnote 1. No effectiveness claim or current policy inference.

facts.statement: Keeping includes possession, control and continuation.
facts.source_detail: Transitive senses 1 and 3; no numerical ranking.

facts.statement: Maintain can preserve an existing state, prevent decline, or continue it.
facts.source_detail: Transitive 1/3; does not require human intention in every context.

facts.statement: Preserve includes protecting against harm or decay and keeping intact.
facts.source_detail: Transitive 1/2.

facts.statement: Withhold can decline to grant, give or permit.
facts.source_detail: Transitive 3; entitlement or a duty to give is not made a necessary condition.

facts.statement: Lose includes deprivation, failure to maintain, and failure to keep in mind.
facts.source_detail: Transitive 2/6/9; object-specific examples in candidate are editorial.

facts.statement: Relinquish can give up possession/control; a forced relinquishment is exemplified.
facts.source_detail: Transitive 2/3b and dictionary example of forced control transfer.

facts.statement: Surrender can yield possession/control under demand or compulsion.
facts.source_detail: Transitive 1a.

facts.statement: Employ includes engaging services and providing paid work.
facts.source_detail: Transitive 1c.

facts.statement: Hire includes engaging personal services for payment.
facts.source_detail: Verb transitive 1a; not restricted to employees.

facts.statement: Engage can arrange use of someone’s services.
facts.source_detail: Transitive 4b with lawyer example.

facts.statement: Dismiss can remove someone from a position or service.
facts.source_detail: Transitive 2.

facts.statement: Release can free someone from confinement, employment or an obligation.
facts.source_detail: Verb (1) senses 1/2; no implication of a particular sports transaction.

facts.statement: Hold includes supporting position, preventing escape and containing.
facts.source_detail: Transitive 4b/5a/6a.

facts.statement: Dissipate can disperse until vanishing; physics includes loss of heat or electricity.
facts.source_detail: Transitive 1b/1c and intransitive 1.

facts.statement: Excrete concerns physiological separation and discharge of waste.
facts.source_detail: General definition and Medical Definition; salt/water details use NIDDK/MSD additionally.

facts.statement: Drain can draw liquid off or remove surplus water.
facts.source_detail: Transitive 1a/2 and intransitive 1/2; not exclusively clinical.

facts.statement: Remember can bring to mind or retain information in memory.
facts.source_detail: Transitive 1/4.

facts.statement: Forget can lose remembrance or fail to recall.
facts.source_detail: Transitive 1a.

facts.statement: Erase includes deleting records and figuratively removing from memory.
facts.source_detail: Transitive 1c/1d/2a; not limited to intentional physical acts.

facts.statement: Memorize means learning something for memory.
facts.source_detail: Transitive definition.

facts.statement: Recall can bring something back to mind.
facts.source_detail: Transitive 2b.

facts.statement: Accumulate can gather or increase gradually in amount.
facts.source_detail: Transitive/intransitive definitions.

facts.statement: Expel can force something outward.
facts.source_detail: Transitive 1, including a lung/smoke example.

facts.statement: Acquire involves obtaining possession or a new characteristic.
facts.source_detail: Transitive 1a/1b.

facts.statement: Promote can advance a student to the next grade.
facts.source_detail: Transitive 1c; distinct from marketing or employment promotion.

facts.statement: Fire meaning dismiss from employment is labelled informal.
facts.source_detail: British English verb sense 27, rather than an unrelated fire sense.

facts.statement: Engage in the employ sense is labelled formal, mainly UK.
facts.source_detail: EMPLOY section, original-publisher search result; not a claim that it is unavailable elsewhere.

facts.statement: Release permits free movement, including gases/energy, and can free someone from obligations.
facts.source_detail: Senses 2 and 8; cited only for the appropriate two contrasts.

sources.title: Collins Easy Learning Idioms: keep something in mind

facts.statement: Keep something in mind concerns remembering an important consideration.
facts.source_detail: Idiom definition; numerical frequency and colloquial ranking not supplied.

facts.statement: Hold somebody back can prevent grade advancement; separate senses hinder progress.
facts.source_detail: School-specific first subentry and hold somebody/something back sense 2; separable displayed frame.

facts.statement: With a separable particle verb, an unstressed personal-pronoun object precedes the particle.
facts.source_detail: Phrasal verbs and objects; retrieved original-publisher search body after direct fetch failed. Applied to Oxford’s hold somebody back frame.
